body:
Source: GitHub issue #674 (release-audit class data-loss, P1-high). Re-verified on main @ 6ddd5992: `packages/lesson-foundry/bin/lesson-foundry.mjs`'s `--write` path (the `realPlan` loop, around line 120-131) does `writeFileSync(fullPath, file.content, 'utf8')` for every planned lint descriptor / generated check script / SKILL.md stub, with NO existence check, no diff, no backup, and no `--force` flag. Hand-refining these artifacts is an EXPECTED workflow step — `packages/lesson-foundry/lib/emit.mjs`/`foundry.mjs` themselves reason about "a pre-overlap or hand-refined lesson" and a filename that "has since drifted or been renamed during refinement", and the README calls the emitted SKILL stub "Ready to load into any skill-mining pipeline" (implying manual polish is the normal next step). Verified: tuning a `.lint.json`'s `pattern` field by hand and adding a `note` field, then running `lesson-foundry --write` again, silently restored the generic scaffold and both hand edits were gone — reported only as an ordinary `wrote:` line, no warning. The SEPARATE interrogation-template path (later in the same file, `templatePlan` loop) already does the right thing: it APPENDS with per-question dedup rather than overwriting — that is the reference behaviour to match in spirit (safe-by-default), though the mechanism differs (skip vs. append) because these are whole-file artifacts, not an appendable log.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/lesson-foundry`: bin/lesson-foundry.mjs (the CLI — the `realPlan` write loop is the one to fix; the `templatePlan` loop right after it is UNRELATED and must not change), lib/{cluster,emit,foundry,llm,report,route}.mjs (the planning logic that PRODUCES `file.content`/`file.path` for `realPlan` entries — do not change what content is planned, only whether it is written). Tests: `npm test -w packages/lesson-foundry` (existing `test/cli.test.mjs` covers the CLI's `--write` behaviour — read it first to see the current fixture/assertion style).

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. In the `realPlan` write loop, before calling `writeFileSync` for each `file`, check `existsSync(fullPath)`. If it already exists: skip the write, print `  exists (skipped): <fullPath>` (text mode) — do not throw, do not opError, this is a normal outcome — and continue to the next file. Track a count of skipped files.
2. Add a `--force` (or `--overwrite`, pick one and be consistent with this repo's existing flag-naming style — check a couple of other packages' `--force`-style flags for the convention) boolean flag, default `false`. When set, restore TODAY'S unconditional-overwrite behaviour exactly (no existence check, no skip message) — this is the explicit opt-in for a deliberate regenerate-everything run.
3. `--json` output includes the skip information too (a `skipped: [<path>, ...]` array or equivalent alongside whatever the JSON report already returns for the write step — read the existing JSON shape in cli.test.mjs / report.mjs first and extend it consistently, do not invent a parallel reporting mechanism).
4. The `templatePlan` (interrogation-template) loop is UNCHANGED — it already appends safely; do not touch it or its dedup logic.
5. `mkdirSync` for the output directory and any per-file write ERROR handling (the existing `opError` on a genuine write failure) are unchanged — this ticket only adds the existence check ahead of the write attempt.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 A second `--write` run against an out-dir where a `.lint.json` was hand-edited: the file is BYTE-IDENTICAL after the run (untouched), and text-mode output shows `  exists (skipped): <path>` for it. verify: `node --test packages/lesson-foundry/test/write-preserve-existing.test.mjs`
- AC2 The SAME scenario with `--force`: the file IS overwritten with the regenerated scaffold (today's behaviour, now opt-in). verify: `node --test packages/lesson-foundry/test/write-preserve-existing.test.mjs`
- AC3 A FRESH out-dir (no existing files) with plain `--write` (no `--force`) writes every planned file exactly as before — the skip logic never blocks a genuinely new file. verify: `node --test packages/lesson-foundry/test/write-preserve-existing.test.mjs`
- AC4 `--json --write` on a mix of new and pre-existing files reports both the written and the skipped paths in the JSON output. verify: `node --test packages/lesson-foundry/test/write-preserve-existing.test.mjs`
- AC5 The interrogation-template append path is unaffected (existing coverage in `test/cli.test.mjs` for that path still passes unmodified). verify: `npm test -w packages/lesson-foundry`
- AC6 Existing suite green (confirm actual baseline count; if any existing test in `test/cli.test.mjs` asserted the OLD unconditional-overwrite as the default `--write` behaviour, update it to use `--force` or assert the new skip behaviour, and say so in the PR body — that would have been pinning the bug). verify: `npm test -w packages/lesson-foundry`
- AC7 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: the alternative `.lint.json.new`-sidecar-file design mentioned in the issue (skip-by-default is the chosen, simpler fix); any change to what content is planned/generated.

PROCESS (ADLC). Work only in your assigned worktree. P3: the rails on this ticket are frozen — if the fix appears to require editing a rail path, STOP and report; never set ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS. P4: TDD — write test/write-preserve-existing.test.mjs first, run it RED, then implement. P5 before opening the PR: the package suite, `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` (exit 0), then the cross-model review loop (see lane instructions) until a round is clean. Do not add gate-manifest entries. Keep the diff to packages/lesson-foundry/bin/lesson-foundry.mjs, the new test, and this ticket's shard. PR title `fix(lesson-foundry): ...`, body must contain `Closes #674`.
title: lesson-foundry: --write skips an existing lint/check/skill artifact by default instead of silently overwriting hand-refined content
